data.one_liner: A Flutter wrapper for Highcharts to render interactive line, column, pie, and combination charts.
data.what_it_does: Renders Highcharts.JS charts inside a Flutter application across mobile, desktop, and web. It supports passing charts either as a JSON configuration string or via a fully typed, generated `HCOptions` API.
use_when: You already use Highcharts in your web stack and want to reuse configurations in Flutter
You need advanced or complex chart types provided by Highcharts JS
You need native client-side chart exporting to PNG, JPEG, or SVG on mobile and desktop
avoid_when: You are targeting Linux (not implemented yet)
You prefer a 100% native Flutter charting library without a webview or JS dependency
You need formatters or JS callbacks that cannot be easily expressed via JSON payloads
strengths: Supports both raw configuration strings and a typed `HCOptions` API
Cross-platform support for Android, iOS, Web, Windows, and macOS
Native saving of chart exports to disk on supported platforms
weaknesses: Linux platform is not implemented and shows an unsupported placeholder
Relies on a WebView wrapper underneath for rendering Highcharts.JS
data.setup_notes: Requires including Highcharts scripts either via CDN (networkScripts) or bundled locally (localScripts). Web platforms require scripts in web/index.html, and macOS requires the downloads entitlement for exporting files.

alternatives.name: fl_chart
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pure Flutter implementation for charts without relying on a webview or JS backend.

alternatives.name: syncfusion_flutter_charts
alternatives.why_pick_it: Comprehensive, high-performance native charts for Flutter with enterprise support.

data.minimal_example:
HighCharts(
  size: const Size(400, 300),
  data: _chartData,
  networkScripts: const [
    'https://code.highcharts.com/highcharts.js',
  ],
)
